title: Prompt-ensemble regression & stability audit — int4/int8 variants
content:
Summary:
This document records a targeted stability and regression audit comparing FP16 baseline to int8 and int4 quantized variants (AWQ and GPTQ toolchains) using a diverse prompt ensemble. The goal was to surface slice-level quality deltas that are not visible in aggregate metrics, and to produce concrete rollout guardrails for canarying quantized models in serving.

Why a prompt-ensemble approach:
- Many regressions are prompt-dependent (templated instructions, few-shot examples, multi-turn state). A single test-suite average masks these effects.
- We clustered prompt templates into 7 ensembles (factual-QA, instruction-summarize, code-completion, multi-turn-chat, conversational-chitchat, math-reasoning, opinion/ambiguous requests) and measured per-ensemble deltas.

Experiment setup (short):
- Models: base open-model-v2 FP16 (baseline), open-model-v2-awq-int4, open-model-v2-gptq-int4, open-model-v2-int8-gptq.
- Prompt ensembles: ~1.2k prompts total (balanced by length & domain).
- Metrics: ROUGE-L, BLEU (where applicable), Exact-Match (factual-QA), embedding-similarity (cosine on SBERT-lite), calibrated hallucination rate (human-labeled subset), token log-prob shift (avg per-token).
- Evaluation mode: deterministic decoding (top-p 0.0 / greedy) for parity across quant variants, plus sample-based checks (top-p 0.9) for diversity tests.
- Hardware: same runtime, batch=1 latency SLO path (we disabled heavy batching to surface worst-case per-token behavior).

Key high-level findings:
1) Aggregate metrics are close: mean embedding-sim delta between FP16 and int8-gptq ~ -0.8 points, AWQ-int4 shows ~ -1.6 points, GPTQ-int4 ~ -1.3 points.
2) Slice-level regressions concentrated in math-reasoning and few-shot code-completion ensembles for int4 variants: exact-match drop in math ~ 4.1% (AWQ-int4) vs baseline, code-completion symptoms include incorrect variable names and truncated tokens.
3) Hallucination rate (human-labeled subset) increases disproportionately for ambiguous-opinion prompts under int4 AWQ: +2.6pp (percentage points) absolute.
4) Token log-prob shift: int4 AWQ shows long-tail negative log-prob shifts on tokens appearing outside training distribution (rare entities), suggesting quantization noise in softmax pre-logit activations.
5) KV-cache replay effect: multi-turn-chat ensemble occasionally repeated prior utterances with int4 AWQ; hypothesis: small numeric drift in KV offsets leading to misaligned attention when sequence length grows > 512.

Representative per-ensemble deltas (FP16 -> AWQ-int4 / GPTQ-int4 / int8-GPTQ):
- factual-QA: EM delta [-0.8%, -0.6%, -0.4%]
- instruction-summarize: ROUGE-L delta [-1.2, -0.9, -0.4]
- code-completion: functional failure cases +3.8% for AWQ-int4 (bugs), GPTQ-int4 +1.9%
- multi-turn-chat: conversational repeat rate +2.0% (AWQ-int4), +0.7% (GPTQ-int4)
- math-reasoning: EM delta [-4.1, -2.7, -1.1]
- chitchat: negligible average delta but higher variance for int4 variants
- ambiguous-opinion: hallucination +2.6pp (AWQ-int4), +1.1pp (GPTQ-int4)

Failure-mode notes and examples (abbreviated):
- Code completion: short function that references 'user_id' becomes 'user_i' or 'userId' inconsistently under AWQ-int4; failing unit tests in synthetic executor in 7/120 cases.
- Math: simple multi-step arithmetic leads to off-by-one on carry operations in ~12/300 prompts for AWQ-int4. Not observed in int8-GPTQ.
- Multi-turn: when context window crosses 512 tokens, int4 variants occasionally re-echo last assistant message; reproduced deterministically by replay script.

Investigation findings (root cause hypotheses):
- AWQ pipeline produces higher activation quantization noise for out-of-distribution tokens due to per-tensor scale heuristics. This amplifies in deeper layers for long sequences.
- GPTQ int4 implementation used blockwise second-order correction that reduces systematic bias, explaining its intermediate performance.
- int8-GPTQ remains closest to FP16 across most slices, suggesting int8 is a safer default for initial canaries.

Operational recommendations for onboarding and rollout:
- Canary strategy: start with int8-GPTQ for route-level canaries with 5–10% traffic, monitor per-route slice metrics (embedding sim, hallucination).
- For int4 variants: require slice-level gating rules before promotion. Block promotion to prod for routes with math-reasoning, code-completion, or multi-turn-chat unless slice delta thresholds met (EM drop < 1% and hallucination delta < 1pp).
- Monitoring hooks: token-logprob drift alert, rolling window hallucination checks (human-in-the-loop sampling at 0.1% traffic), and KV-cache integrity probes that intentionally push >512 tokens to detect echo regressions.
- Fallback policy: automatic fallback to FP16 or int8-GPTQ for any route that exceeds hallucination threshold or EM degradation for > 30 mins.

Short checklist for next actions (owner assignments):
- Re-run AWQ with alternative per-channel scaling heuristics (Maya) — target: reduce rare-token logprob drift.
- Expand human-labeled hallucination set to 2k examples representing ambiguous-opinion slice (Lina).
- Add deterministic KV-cache stress tests to CI with varying prefixes and token lengths (Jamal).
- Prepare a canary playbook and dashboard tiles for per-slice metrics (Omar).

Appendix: sample prompts from ensembles (truncated)
- math-reasoning: "Compute 47+58 then multiply by 3 and subtract the initial sum."
- code-completion: "Complete the function that returns user profile JSON given args: name, user_id, email."
- multi-turn-chat: "User: remind me later. Assistant: OK, when should I remind you? User: in two weeks. Assistant:..."

Notes: this is intended as a working audit to inform a safe rollout. Many findings are reproducible via the eval harness linked above; follow-ups should iterate on quantization config and re-run the same prompt-ensemble to validate regression closures.
